intro.data: A process turns one thing into another. Your toolkit holds two machines that both accept the messy spreadsheet — but they do different things to it. Bring the one you trust onto the board, wire it from the input to the clean table, and leave the other in the tray.
intro.alchemy: A process turns one material into another. Your toolkit holds two apparatuses that both accept the raw ore — but they do different things to it. Bring the one you trust onto the board, wire it from the ore to the pure ingot, and leave the other in the tray.
intro.spellcraft: A working turns one essence into another. Your toolkit holds two runes that both accept the wild spark — but they do different things to it. Bring the one you trust onto the board, wire it from the spark to the steady flame, and leave the other in the tray.
intro.abstract: A morphism turns one object into another. Your toolkit holds two machines of the same type A → B that behave differently: f sends a ↦ b, g sends a ↦ b′. Place the one that yields the goal value b and wire it from the input.

goal.data: Drag the machine you need onto the board and wire the input through it to the clean table.
goal.alchemy: Drag the apparatus you need onto the board and wire the ore through it to the pure ingot.
goal.spellcraft: Drag the rune you need onto the board and wire the spark through it to the steady flame.
goal.abstract: Place and wire the machine that sends the input a to the goal value b.

afterSuccess.data: You watched the messy spreadsheet become a clean table. Both machines were the same type, but only one behaved the way you wanted — a process is defined by what it does, not just what it connects.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You watched the raw ore become a pure ingot. Both apparatuses were the same type, but only one behaved the way you wanted — a process is defined by what it does.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You watched the wild spark become a steady flame. Both runes were the same type, but only one behaved the way you wanted — a working is defined by what it does.
afterSuccess.abstract: The input became the goal value. Same-typed morphisms can do different things; a morphism is defined by its behavior.

reveal.summary: The things being transformed are objects; the process between them is an arrow, or morphism. Two morphisms with the same source and target can still behave differently.
reveal.moreFormal: A morphism f: A → B has one source and one target. Knowing its type (A → B) is not the same as knowing what it does.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: f: (input: A) => B — two functions with the same signature can compute different things.
